one_month_reasoning: No company earnings in the window: Q1 FY27 results are expected ~Nov 5-6, 2026 (unconfirmed) [16]. Scheduled in-window items: Oct 27-28 FOMC, where Kalshi/Polymarket price ~72-74% hold vs ~27-28% a second hike after the Sep 16 hike [8] (hold would be mild relief for a debt-funded, long-duration name; the 10y at 5.29% [9] is already a headwind); September CPI/jobs prints; possible unscheduled 2027-capacity contract signings (mgmt says late-stage [2], an upside skew) and Horizon 2-4 Microsoft delivery updates. Momentum is negative (-10% since Sep 24 on Rothschild Neutral $40 and a B. Riley PT cut) and peers CRWV/CIFR/WULF are flat-to-down over Jul-Sep [11]. These roughly offset, so I centre on today's $40.65 with monthly sigma ~0.29 (slightly below 107%/3.5 because volume is fading and no earnings sit in the window).

fair_value.method: Blend of DCF $36 (40%: WACC 11.5%, g 3%, 1.5GW terminal at $17M rev/MW, 70% margin, $44M/MW capex), EV/EBITDA $53.5 (30%: $5.0B NTM EBITDA x 8x less $15.3B net debt) and EV/contracted-ARR $25.3 (30%: $9B x 3.0x) = ~$38 per share at Oct 2027.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FCFF FY27-FY31 + Gordon terminal; WACC 11.5%, g 3%; revenue $2.8B/$7.3B/$15.2B/$19.0B/$23.0B (FY27-31), EBITDA margin 70% (FY27 75% consensus), capex FY27 $27.5B then 0.2GW/yr at $44M/MW; terminal 1.5GW IT at $17M rev/MW, GPU $34M/MW over 5.5 yrs; 50% of FY27 GPU capex prepaid, unwound over 5 yrs; net debt $1.70B; 394.1M shares; PV now $31.0/sh x (1+Ke 16%) = $36 at Oct-2027. Sensitivity: terminal rev/MW $16M -> $18, $18M -> $54; margin 65% -> ~-$10, 75% -> ~$47 (5-yr GPU life).

bear.story: AI-capex digestion / 'telecom 2000' analog [20]: GPU rental prices keep falling [19], 2027 capacity goes unsold or reprices below $15M/MW, $25-30B capex forces equity raises near lows while rates stay high (10y >5% [9], Fed hiking [8]); EV/ARR compresses to ~2x on a much bigger debt stack.

base.story: $4B ARR goes live by Dec 2026, part of the 2027 0.5GW is contracted at ~$20M/MW, Microsoft Horizons run on schedule; dilution and debt offset growth, so the stock ends near fair value (~$38-42), in line with the sector's flat-to-down 2026.

bull.story: All 2027 capacity signed at $20-25M/MW with IG customers and prepayments, ARR heads toward $10B+, market re-rates IREN to Nebius-like multiples (~15x forward EBITDA [18]) and back above the $76.87 high; prediction markets keep AI-bust odds low [7].

thesis_break_reason: At $24 the market cap (~$9.5B) plus $1.7B net debt is ~2.8x the $4B already-contracted ARR, the financefeeds bear multiple [4], with no value for the 2027 build or the 5GW grid pipeline. Trading there would most likely mean a funding problem (failed GPU financing, distressed equity raise), contract slippage/cancellation or a broken GPU-pricing regime, not ordinary volatility. It is also well below the July 2026 low of $28.93.

reasoning: Facts: FY26 revenue $707M; Q4 AI cloud $70.5M; $4B contracted ARR for 2026 capacity, $1B operating; FY27 capex guided $25-30B; debt $7.59B vs cash $5.90B; 394M shares [1,2,3,13]. Base rates: (1) IREN's history is a poor anchor for drift (rolling 12m returns from 2021 span -80% to +450%, median +63%, a small-cap/bitcoin-era regime), but it does say vol stays very high: realized 87-107% over the last 1-2 yrs [10]. I use sigma ~0.80 for the 12-month lognormal, trimmed for the larger cap and contracted revenue. (2) Peers: CRWV -35% y/y, CIFR +23%, WULF +31%, and all fell 35-45% from June 2026 highs alongside IREN [11], in step with the Sep 16 Fed hike and a 10y at 5.29% [8,9]. That is a sector re-rating, not an IREN-specific break. (3) Multiples: IREN's value/ARR compressed from 6.4x to 4.35x as 39% dilution hit per-share value [4]; CRWV trades ~7-8x EBITDA, NBIS ~15x [5,18]. (4) Macro/event odds: Polymarket AI-bubble-burst ~8% by Dec-2026 and ~18% by Jun-2027 [7]; telecom-2000 analog says equity damage leads defaults by 1-2 yrs [20]; GPU rental deflation ~75% for H100s [19] argues against capitalizing today's $20-25M/MW pricing forever. Valuation: blended FV ~$38 (DCF $36, EV/EBITDA $53.5, EV/ARR $25). The DCF is extremely sensitive to terminal $/MW and GPU life, which is why I don't lean on the sell-side mean PT of ~$78 [12], a level that has historically run far ahead of outcomes in high-vol names. Ladder: lognormal, median ~$38.5 (slightly below spot, matching FV, dilution drag and a high-rate tape), sigma 0.80, with a slightly fatter left tail for a funding-stress outcome (P(<$10) ~6%) and a trimmed far-right tail. Implied P(up) ~47%, mean ~$52 because of right skew. Research limits: Twelve Data stats/estimates/earnings endpoints and Alpha Vantage were unavailable (plan/rate limits), Kalshi direct page returned 429 so market volume for the Fed contract is not quoted, and X was not used.
